questions.question: Analyze the relationship between heavy television viewing and perceptions of reality. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Analyze the relationship between heavy television viewing and perceptions of reality.
  • [K] / [CO3]
  • Heavy television viewing influences how people perceive reality, as explained by George
  • Gerbner’s Cultivation Theory. Continuous exposure to television content gradually shapes
  • viewers’ beliefs about the world. Frequent viewers tend to accept televised images, values,
  • and social patterns as real, even when they are exaggerated. This often results in distorted
  • perceptions of social reality, such as overestimating crime, violence, or stereotypes, making
  • television a powerful cultivator of attitudes and worldviews.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Outline how signs convey meaning in advertisements or films. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Outline how signs convey meaning in advertisements or films. [A] / [CO4]
  • Signs in advertisements or films communicate meaning by using visual, auditory, and textual
  • elements that represent ideas or emotions. Images, colours, and symbols evoke specific
  • feelings, while music and sound effects create mood and enhance narrative impact. For
  • example, red may signify passion or danger, while upbeat music can create excitement.
  • Logos or cultural symbols connect audiences to brands or social contexts. Words and slogans
  • complement visuals to reinforce meaning. The combination of these signs enables audiences
  • to quickly interpret messages, relate to content emotionally, and understand the intended
  • message effectively.

questions.question: Summarize a short note on how Newcomb’s model emphasizes communication as a social process. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Summarize a short note on how Newcomb’s model emphasizes communication as a
  • social process. [K] / [CO2]
  • Newcomb’s Model emphasizes communication as a social process by focusing on
  • relationships and shared understanding. Proposed by Theodore M. Newcomb in 1953, the
  • ABX model explains how communication occurs between two individuals (A and B) about
  • an object or issue (X) to maintain balance in attitudes. When imbalance or disagreement
  • arises, communication helps reduce tension and restore harmony. Thus, the model highlights
  • interpersonal interaction, mutual influence, and the role of communication in maintaining
  • social equilibrium rather than mass communication.
  • .

questions.question: Explain non-verbal communication and illustrate it with examples from daily life. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain non-verbal communication and illustrate it with examples from daily life.
  • [U] / [CO1]
  • Non-verbal communication conveys messages without words, using body language, gestures,
  • facial expressions, posture, eye contact, and proxemics. For instance, a smile indicates
  • friendliness, while a frown shows displeasure. Nodding communicates agreement, and a firm
  • handshake conveys confidence. Eye contact signals attention and honesty, while avoiding it
  • may suggest discomfort. Posture reflects attitude; standing straight shows confidence, while
  • slouching indicates disinterest. Touch, such as a pat on the back, communicates support.
  • Even silence can express thoughtfulness or disagreement. Non-verbal cues complement
  • verbal messages and are essential in daily interactions to express emotions and intentions
  • clearly.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: What is the difference between traditional and digital mass media? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• What is the difference between traditional and digital mass media? [U] / [CO1]
  • Traditional mass media includes newspapers, radio, and television, which deliver messages in
  • a one-way format to passive audiences. It primarily informs or entertains but offers limited
  • interaction. Digital mass media, such as social media platforms, websites, and streaming
  • services, enables two-way communication, allowing users to respond, comment, share, and
  • create content. Digital media is faster, accessible globally, and interactive, while traditional
  • media often follows scheduled programming and localized reach. Additionally, digital
  • platforms track engagement, allowing personalized experiences. The key difference lies in
  • interactivity, accessibility, speed, and the level of audience participation between the two.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Describe the functions of mass media with suitable examples. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the functions of mass media with suitable examples. [U] / [CO1]
  • The media plays a crucial role in society by informing people about current events,
  • educating through formal and informal learning, and entertaining audiences via films,
  • shows, and music. It also persuades and influences public opinion through advertisements,
  • campaigns, and editorials. As a watchdog, media monitors governments and institutions,
  • exposing corruption and safeguarding public interest, which is why it is called the Fourth
  • Estate in a democracy. Media aids socialization by shaping values, norms, and behavior, and
  • supports cultural transmission by preserving traditions and introducing global cultures.
  • Finally, it acts as a catalyst for development, promoting health, education, awareness, and
  • social progress.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Illustrate how people share information effectively through interpersonal communication. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Illustrate how people share information effectively through interpersonal
  • communication. [U] / [CO1]
  • Interpersonal communication is the direct exchange of information between two or more
  • individuals. It relies on verbal and non-verbal cues to ensure clarity and understanding.
  • Effective communication involves active listening, feedback, and clarification to prevent
  • misunderstandings. For example, colleagues discussing a project share ideas, resolve doubts,
  • and coordinate tasks. Emotional expression, tone, and body language help convey attitudes
  • and intentions. Face-to-face interactions, phone calls, or video conferences allow participants
  • to respond immediately. By combining verbal and non-verbal elements, interpersonal
  • communication enables precise, timely, and meaningful sharing of information in personal,
  • professional, and social contexts.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Explain group communication and discuss its importance in teamwork and decision-making. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain group communication and discuss its importance in teamwork and decision-
  • making. [U]/ [CO1]
  • Group communication involves interaction among three or more individuals working toward
  • a common goal. It allows members to share ideas, discuss problems, and collaborate
  • effectively. Open communication promotes understanding, prevents misunderstandings, and
  • encourages diverse perspectives. In teamwork, group communication builds trust,
  • coordination, and accountability among members. During decision-making, discussions and
  • debates help evaluate alternatives, identify solutions, and achieve consensus. For example, a
  • team planning a marketing campaign shares creative ideas, delegates tasks, and finalizes
  • strategies collaboratively. Effective group communication enhances productivity, problem-
  • solving, and cohesion, ensuring that team objectives are achieved efficiently and
  • harmoniously.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Write a short note on the importance of the effect component in Lasswell’s model. / [CO2] [5x5 = 25] Part D ESSAY Each question carries 15 marks
questions.solution_html:
• Write a short note on the importance of the effect component in Lasswell’s model.
  • [K] / [CO2]
  • The effect component in Lasswell’s communication model examines the impact of a message
  • on its audience. It evaluates whether communication has influenced knowledge, attitudes,
  • beliefs, or behaviour. By measuring effects, communicators can assess the success of
  • campaigns, advertisements, or public messages. For example, a health awareness campaign
  • can be evaluated by changes in vaccination rates or public awareness. The effect component
  • also guides future communication strategies, helping refine content, methods, and channels
  • for better results. Understanding effects ensures that communication is purposeful, targeted,
  • and capable of achieving desired outcomes in social, educational, or political contexts.
  • Part D
  • ESSAY
  • Each question carries 15 marks

questions.question: Explain the concept of dysfunctions of media. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the concept of dysfunctions of media. [U] / [CO1]
  • Dysfunctions of media refer to the negative or unintended effects that occur when
  • communication fails, leading to confusion, conflict, manipulation, or misinformation instead
  • of clarity and understanding. Examples include the spread of rumours, fake news, and
  • distorted representations of reality.
